input: Find bribery and market-manipulation enforcement actions involving Glencore since 2018

entity.group: Glencore Group (Glencore International A.G.; listed as Glencore plc)
entity.hq_country: Switzerland (incorporated in Jersey; domiciled in Baar, Switzerland)

events.parties: Glencore plc subsidiary (documents demand on behalf of DOJ)
events.summary: US DOJ subpoenaed a Glencore subsidiary for documents on FCPA and money-laundering compliance concerning business in Nigeria, the DRC and Venezuela from 2007 onward, opening the US criminal probe that ended in the May 2022 guilty pleas.

events.type: Bribery / money laundering – individual guilty plea
events.parties: Anthony Stimler, former Glencore West Africa crude oil desk trader
events.summary: Former Glencore trader Anthony Stimler pleaded guilty in the US to one count of conspiracy to violate the FCPA and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering for his role in paying bribes, and cooperated with the investigation.

events.parties: Emilio Jose Heredia Collado, former senior fuel oil trader at Glencore Ltd
events.summary: A former Glencore Ltd senior fuel oil trader pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to engage in commodities price manipulation tied to the Platts fuel-oil benchmark scheme.

events.amount: more than US$30 million in bribes to Petrobras employees (2011-2014, figure covering Glencore, Vitol and Trafigura jointly)
events.status: investigated (later resolved for Glencore via 2022 Brazil settlement)
events.parties: Glencore International A.G. (with Vitol and Trafigura)
events.summary: Brazilian federal prosecutors said Glencore was among three trading houses that paid more than $30 million in bribes to Petrobras employees in over 160 operations between 2011 and 2014.

events.status: investigated (company strand resolved 2022; individual strand ongoing)
events.parties: Glencore Group of companies, its officials, employees, agents and associated persons
events.summary: The UK SFO opened a criminal investigation into the Glencore Group for bribery, covering South Sudan and other countries (commenced 12 June 2019, Glencore informed 5 December 2019).

events.type: Foreign bribery – corporate criminal conviction (FCPA conspiracy)
events.amount: US$428,521,173 criminal fine + US$272,185,792 forfeiture/disgorgement (~US$700m total at sentencing incl. US$29.6m restitution)
events.summary: Glencore International A.G. pleaded guilty in SDNY to conspiracy to violate the FCPA, admitting more than $100 million paid through intermediaries in 2007-2018 to bribe officials in Nigeria, Cameroon, Ivory Coast, Equatorial Guinea, Brazil, Venezuela and the DRC; sentenced in February 2023 to a ~$700 million payment, $29.6 million restitution and five years' probation.

events.amount: US$341,221,682 criminal fine + US$144,417,203 criminal forfeiture
events.summary: Glencore Ltd. pleaded guilty in the District of Connecticut to conspiracy to engage in commodity price manipulation, admitting manipulation or attempted manipulation of S&P Global Platts fuel-oil benchmark price assessments (Los Angeles 380 CST bunker fuel and Houston high-sulfur fuel oil) from about January 2011 to August 2019, including a bilateral scheme with 'Company A' between September 2012 and August 2016.

events.type: Market manipulation and corruption – civil enforcement order
events.amount: US$1.186 billion (US$865,630,784 civil monetary penalty + US$320,715,066 disgorgement) – largest in CFTC history
events.parties: Glencore International A.G., Glencore Ltd., Chemoil Corporation
events.summary: The CFTC ordered Glencore and its affiliates to pay $1.186 billion for manipulating or attempting to manipulate four US-based S&P Global Platts physical oil benchmarks and related futures and swaps on hundreds of days (2007-2018) and for fraud and corrupt payments to employees and agents of state-owned entities in Brazil, Cameroon, Nigeria, Venezuela and Mexico.

events.type: Bribery – corporate criminal conviction (UK Bribery Act 2010)
events.parties: Glencore Energy UK Ltd (wholly-owned UK subsidiary)
events.summary: Glencore Energy UK Ltd pleaded guilty to seven counts (five of bribery under s.1 and two of failure to prevent bribery under s.7 of the Bribery Act 2010) for paying about $29 million in bribes to gain preferential access to oil in Nigeria, Cameroon, Ivory Coast, Equatorial Guinea and South Sudan; Southwark Crown Court ordered it to pay £280,965,092.95 on 3 November 2022 — the first conviction of a UK company for authorising active bribery under s.1 of the Bribery Act.
Glencore International A.G. agreed to pay $39,598,367 to the Brazilian Federal Prosecutor's Office (MPF) to resolve bribery allegations concerning Petrobras arising from Operation Car Wash.

events.parties: Glencore Group / Glencore International A.G. and the DRC government
events.summary: Glencore agreed to pay the Democratic Republic of Congo $180 million, covering all present and future claims for alleged acts of corruption by the Glencore Group in the DRC between 2007 and 2018.

events.type: Bribery – corporate criminal conviction (summary penalty order)
events.amount: CHF 2 million fine plus compensation claim of US$150 million (~US$179.7m total including other claims)
events.summary: Switzerland's Office of the Attorney General found Glencore guilty of inadequate organisation (Art. 102 SCC) in connection with bribery of foreign public officials (Art. 322septies SCC) over corrupt DRC mine deals — the Mutanda and Kansuki acquisitions routed through Dan Gertler in 2011, with about $26 million transferred to Gertler-controlled Swiss accounts.
Nigeria announced a $50 million settlement with Glencore International A.G. over bribery, following the company's earlier US, UK and Brazilian resolutions.

events.type: Bribery / falsification of accounts – individual prosecution
events.status: charged (not-guilty pleas entered; trial listed 4 October 2027)
events.parties: Six former Glencore employees: Martin Wakefield, David Perez, Alex Beard, Andrew Gibson, Paul Hopkirk, Ramon Labiaga
events.summary: The SFO charged six former Glencore employees with conspiring to make corrupt payments benefiting Glencore's oil operations in Cameroon, Nigeria and Ivory Coast (2007-2014); four pleaded not guilty at Southwark Crown Court on 10 November 2025 and Beard and Gibson on 10 September 2026, with a trial listed for October 2027; Gibson, Wakefield and Perez also face conspiracy-to-falsify-documents charges over invoices disguised as service fees to a Nigerian oil consultancy.

events.type: Enforcement follow-up – termination of compliance monitorships
events.parties: Glencore plc / Glencore International A.G. and Glencore Ltd; US DOJ
events.summary: DOJ ended the two independent compliance monitorships (SDNY and District of Connecticut) imposed under Glencore's 2022 foreign-bribery and market-manipulation settlements with immediate effect, ending them about three years into the three-year terms.

output.assessment: Glencore has paid more than US$1.5 billion to close the most consequential bribery and market-manipulation probes of the last decade: criminal convictions in the US (2022 FCPA and price-fixing pleas, ~$700m plus a separate $341m fine), the UK (first-ever s.1 Bribery Act corporate conviction, £281m) and Switzerland (2024 summary penalty order), plus settlements with the CFTC ($1.186bn), Brazil, the DRC ($180m) and Nigeria ($50m). DOJ terminated both compliance monitorships early in March 2025, signalling improved cooperation and compliance, and enforcement pressure has since eased. The main open items are the SFO's October 2027 trial of six former Glencore employees in the UK, the outcome of the Swiss compensation claim (~$150m) and any residual Dutch and Swiss follow-on proceedings.
missing_fields: current status/outcome of the Dutch Public Prosecution Service investigation of Glencore (last confirmed 'ongoing' in the company's 24 May 2022 statement)
final disposition (sentencing/status) of US cases against individual Glencore traders other than the guilty pleas of Stimler and Heredia Collado

excluded_namesakes.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co. precious-metals traders (Nowak, Smith, Jordan) and Scotiabank metals-trader DPA
excluded_namesakes.reason: Surfaced in searches for 'Glencore precious metals market manipulation' but are separate banks' metals-desk enforcement actions, not Glencore entities or people

excluded_namesakes.name: Platinum Partners (fraud indictment)
excluded_namesakes.reason: Appeared in searches for 'Glencore market manipulation indictment'; an unrelated investment-fraud case with 'platinum' in its name, no link to Glencore

excluded_namesakes.name: Fleurette Properties (DRC bribery penalty order, March 2026)
excluded_namesakes.reason: Glencore-linked via Dan Gertler's DRC mine deals, but the ~$30m Dutch penalty was imposed on Fleurette Properties, a separate company, not on any Glencore entity
